title: Quest Log data
description: Data format for Quest Log, a project tracker shown as a side-scrolling platformer game. Data lives in a folder tree under data/: one folder per PROJECT (completely unrelated efforts, e.g. 'house-renovation' vs 'work-launch'), holding project.json; one sub-folder per WORLD (a theme within the project) holding world.json; and one file per LEVEL (one key deliverable) in the world folder, named <level-id>.json. Paths: data/<project-id>/project.json, data/<project-id>/<world-id>/world.json, data/<project-id>/<world-id>/<level-id>.json. An optional data/settings.json holds repo-wide display settings, and an optional data/inbox.json holds captured ideas not yet placed in a level. Folder and file names must equal the ids inside. Design principle: 'good enough' beats perfect. Keep MVP criteria minimal; put nice-to-haves in 'stretch' items or non-MVP criteria.

Id.description: Stable identifier in lowercase kebab-case (letters, digits, single hyphens). Also used as folder/file names. Unique within its scope: projects across the repo, worlds within a project, levels within a world, items and criteria within a level. Never reuse or rename once created.

Title.description: Short human-readable name. Imperative for tasks ('Write API docs'), noun phrase for deliverables ('Public beta').

Money.description: An amount of cash in the project's currency, in whole units with up to 2 decimal places (49.99 means £49.99 for GBP, not pence).

Currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code in capitals, e.g. GBP, EUR, USD.

BudgetSettings.description: Optional cash budgets for a project. Its presence turns them on; every field inside has a default, so {} is fine.

currency.description: Currency for every budget and cost in this project. Omit for GBP.

alerts.description: true (default) = alert when a logged cost takes an item, step, level or world past alertAt or over its budget. false = no alerts; budgets still show.

alertAt.description: Percentage of a budget that, once spent, gives a heads-up alert (default 90). Going over the budget always alerts while alerts are on.

Goal.description: A key project goal shown on the Overworld. Worlds reference goals they contribute to.

Project.description: A project: one self-contained effort, stored at data/<project-id>/project.json. Its map (the overworld) shows its key goals and its worlds in order. Projects never reference each other.

$schema.description: Pointer to this schema for editor tooling.

id.description: Project id. Must equal the project folder name: data/<id>/project.json.

archivedAt.description: When the project was archived (put on the shelf). An archived project is off the bedroom floor and its clocks are frozen at this moment: it drops out of Today, the weekly review and every deadline alert, but its history still counts in the stats. Archiving works on unfinished projects too. To unarchive, add the days since archivedAt to pausedDays on every started, uncleared level, then remove this field. Omit for projects in play.

budgets.description: Turns on cash budgets for this project. Omit it and the app hides every budget, cost and alert, even if items carry 'budget' or 'spent' (they are kept for when it's turned back on).

worldOrder.description: World ids in the order they appear on the overworld path. Every id here must have data/<project-id>/<world-id>/world.json. Worlds left out still count: they go after the listed ones, sorted by id, and the app adds them here on its next save. So to add a world, just create its world.json; only edit this list to change the order (editing it is what makes two pull requests conflict).

Theme.description: Visual theme of a world. Pick one matching the world's topic mood.

oneOf.description: Green hills. Default, general work.
Sand and pyramids. Long slogs, infrastructure.
Ocean. Research, exploration, discovery.
Snow. Cleanup, hardening, maintenance.
Clouds. Vision, design, big ideas.
Lava castle. Launches, final pushes, high-stakes work.

World.description: A themed group of levels inside a project (e.g. 'Kitchen', 'Payments'), stored at data/<project-id>/<world-id>/world.json. Its levels are separate files in the same folder.

$schema.description: Pointer to this schema for editor tooling.

id.description: World id. Must equal the world folder name.

goalIds.description: Ids of goals in this project's project.json that this world contributes to.

unlocksAfter.description: Optional ids of other worlds IN THE SAME PROJECT that should be cleared first. Purely visual (world is shown locked), never prevents editing.

budget.description: Optional cash allowance for the whole world. Without it, the world's budget is the sum of its levels' budgets. What's left is banked as savings once every level is cleared.

levelOrder.description: Level ids in play order. Each id must have a file data/<project-id>/<world-id>/<level-id>.json. Level files left out still count: they go after the listed ones, sorted by id, and the app adds them here on its next save. So to add a level, just create its file; only edit this list to change the order (editing it is what makes two pull requests conflict).

Level.description: One key deliverable, stored at data/<project-id>/<world-id>/<level-id>.json. The level is CLEARED when every MVP success criterion is done. Keep MVP criteria to the minimum that makes the deliverable useful.

$schema.description: Pointer to this schema for editor tooling.

id.description: Level id. Must equal the file name without .json. 'world' is reserved (it is the world.json file).

deliverable.description: One sentence: what exists when this level is cleared.
examples: A signup page that creates accounts in production

timeboxDays.description: Time budget in days, counted from startedAt. Finishing early earns bonus XP; running over costs a star.

startedAt.description: When work began. Set automatically when the first item moves to doing/done. Omit for levels not yet started.

clearedAt.description: When all MVP criteria were first done. Set automatically. Omit for uncleared levels.

pausedDays.description: Days this level's clock was suspended while its project was archived. They push the time-box deadline back, so archived time never counts as overdue. Added when the project is unarchived (days from the project's archivedAt to now, for started, uncleared levels). Omit when 0.

someday.description: true = parked on the someday shelf (from the weekly review): the level isn't being worked on, so it drops out of Today, the review's overdue/stale lists and 'next level' suggestions. Parking clears startedAt, so the time-box starts afresh when work resumes; marking an item doing/done or ticking a criterion unparks it. Omit when false.

budget.description: Optional cash allowance for this level. Without it, the level's budget is the sum of its items' budgets. Whatever is left when the level clears is banked as savings.

successCriteria.description: Checks that decide the level is done. At least one must have mvp=true. MVP criteria raise the flagpole; non-MVP criteria are bonus coins.

items.description: Project items placed along the level, left to right by dependency order.

Criterion.description: A success criterion: an observable check that the deliverable is good enough.

examples: A new user can sign up and log in

mvp.description: true = required to clear the level. false = nice-to-have bonus.

done.description: Whether the criterion is currently met.

doneAt.description: When this criterion was last ticked. Set automatically when done becomes true and removed when it is un-ticked. Feeds the stats page's progress calendar and streaks. Optional: older data won't have it.

ItemType.description: What kind of project item this is. Determines how it looks and behaves in the level.

oneOf.description: A piece of work you do. Shown as a ? block; completing it pops a coin.
An intermediate output or milestone inside the level. Shown as a checkpoint flag.
Something stopping progress that must be resolved. Shown as a brick wall; the hero cannot pass until done or dropped.

Something you need from another team, level or external party. Plain: a pipe with a plant while unmet. With 'levelRef': a cloud that carries the hero to that level. With 'subtasks': a warp pipe down to a bonus sub-level of those steps.
Something that might go wrong. Shown as a patrolling critter; 'done' means mitigated or accepted.
An open question needing a decision. Shown as a signpost; the hero waits until decided.
Nice-to-have extra. Shown as floating coins. Never blocks, never earns stars. Put polish here.
Not started.
In progress.
Finished (for risks: mitigated; for decisions: decided; for blockers/dependencies: resolved).
Deliberately cut from scope. Counts as out of the way; cutting scope is encouraged.

Item.description: A project item placed in a level.

doneAt.description: When this item was last marked done. Set automatically when status becomes 'done' and removed when it changes away from done. Feeds the weekly review's "shipped this week". Optional: older data won't have it.

mvp.description: true (default) = on the critical path: the hero stops here until it is done or dropped. false = optional. Ignored for 'stretch' (never MVP).

dependsOn.description: Ids of other items IN THE SAME LEVEL FILE that must come first. Determines left-to-right placement. Must not form cycles.

levelRef.description: For dependency items: another level IN THE SAME PROJECT this depends on, as '<world-id>/<level-id>'. Rendered as a cloud that carries the hero to that level. Don't combine with 'subtasks'.

subtasks.description: For dependency items: the steps needed to get it, when you have to chase it yourself. Rendered as a warp pipe down into a bonus sub-level holding these; clearing them brings the hero back up. Don't combine with 'levelRef'. Omit when the dependency is just something to wait for.

budget.description: Optional estimated cost: the cash set aside for this item. For a dependency with subtasks, it replaces the sum of its steps' budgets. Savings (budget minus spent) are banked when it is done or dropped, so dropping it banks whatever wasn't spent.

spent.description: Optional cash actually spent on this item so far. Fill it in as receipts come in, before or after it is done. For a dependency, it adds to whatever its steps spent.

link.description: Optional URL to a ticket, doc or PR.

SubtaskType.description: Item types allowed inside a dependency's sub-level: any type except 'dependency' (sub-levels don't nest).

oneOf.description: A piece of work you do. Shown as a ? block; completing it pops a coin.
An intermediate output or milestone inside the level. Shown as a checkpoint flag.
Something stopping progress that must be resolved. Shown as a brick wall; the hero cannot pass until done or dropped.
Something that might go wrong. Shown as a patrolling critter; 'done' means mitigated or accepted.
An open question needing a decision. Shown as a signpost; the hero waits until decided.
Nice-to-have extra. Shown as floating coins. Never blocks, never earns stars. Put polish here.

Subtask.description: A step inside a dependency's sub-level. Like an item, but it can't be a dependency itself.

doneAt.description: When this step was last marked done. Set automatically when status becomes 'done' and removed when it changes away from done. Feeds the weekly review's "shipped this week". Optional: older data won't have it.

mvp.description: true (default) = needed to close the dependency. false = optional. Ignored for 'stretch'.

dependsOn.description: Ids of OTHER SUBTASKS OF THE SAME DEPENDENCY that must come first. Must not form cycles.

budget.description: Optional estimated cost of this step. Adds up into the dependency's budget unless the dependency sets its own.

spent.description: Optional cash actually spent on this step so far.

link.description: Optional URL to a ticket, doc or PR.

LevelStats.description: Anti-perfectionism counters. Maintained automatically by the app; tools generating data should omit this.

editsAfterClear.description: Edits made to the level after it was cleared.

itemsAddedAfterClear.description: Items added after the level was cleared (scope creep).

itemEdits.description: Map of item id (or dependency/step for a sub-level step) to number of edits made after that item was done.

timeboxExtendedDays.description: Days added to timeboxDays after the level started (the weekly review's 'extend the time-box'). The in-time star and the time bonus are still scored against the original time-box (timeboxDays minus this).

ItemEditKey.description: An item id, or "<dependency>/<step>" for a step inside a dependency's sub-level.

HeroId.description: Which player character walks the levels.

Settings.description: Repo-wide display settings, stored at data/settings.json. Optional: without it the app uses its defaults.
